title: Students and trade unionists protest school conditions in Paris
seoTitle: Paris student protest over school conditions

tea.why: Students and trade unionists are demonstrating against overcrowded classrooms, deteriorating school infrastructure, and teacher shortages.
tea.want: Demonstrators are demanding better-resourced schools, improved education, a wealth tax, and the voting age lowered to 16.
tea.changed: Oct 16: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused La France Insoumise of exploiting student unrest for electoral advantage.

summary: Students and trade unionists have engaged in ongoing demonstrations across France, including Paris, to protest against poor school conditions, overcrowded classrooms, deteriorating infrastructure, and teacher shortages. The protests, which have involved school blockades and marches, have drawn support from parents and political figures, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused the radical-left La France Insoumise of exploiting the student movement for electoral gain. The demonstrations have faced a heavy security response, leading to widespread arrests and injuries among protesters, teachers, and police officers. Further demonstrations involving trade unions and other groups are planned.
response: According to the sources, the government deployed internal security forces, resulting in mass arrests and clashes. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused political opponents of instrumentalising the high school movement, while police reported that officers and school staff were injured by violent individuals within the crowds.

arrests.text: the vast majority of the 8,000 people arrested in recent weeks are under 18

updates.text: Students marched in Paris to protest against under-resourced schools.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused La France Insoumise of exploiting the high school movement.
Reports highlighted nationwide arrests and injuries as police faced student demonstrations.
